slides.title: CareCompass  |  Alexa+ MCP for medical bills & care barriers
slides.label: Simulated Alexa+ experience
lines: "Alexa, I got an ER bill. What do I actually owe?"
CareCompass: every number you hear is computed, not guessed.
slides.say: Alexa, I got an E R bill. What do I actually owe? Large language models are fluent, but they're bad at money. CareCompass makes sure every dollar Alexa says out loud was computed, not guessed.

slides.title: Architecture
slides.label: Simulated Alexa+ experience
lines: Alexa+ (simulated voice turn, free LLM via OpenRouter :free)
Grounding guard: any $ amount not in a tool result is BLOCKED
-> Alexa reads the server's deterministic speech instead.
All tools read-only. No PHI identifiers.
slides.say: Here's the architecture. A simulated Alexa plus voice turn talks to the CareCompass MCP server over streamable H T T P. The server exposes three read-only tools: a deterministic bill estimator, an interest-free payment plan, and a care barrier screener. On the way back, a grounding guard checks every dollar amount. If a number didn't come from a tool, it's blocked.

slides.title: Live run: the ER bill
slides.label: Simulated Alexa+ experience
lines: Alexa: "Your total patient responsibility is $551.00. You can split
this into 3 equal monthly payments of about $183.67 each,
slides.say: Now a live run. We start the server, then the Alexa simulator. A free Nemotron model picks the tools. It calls estimate patient bill with a five hundred dollar deductible and twenty percent coinsurance. The server does the math: five hundred fifty one dollars. Then payment plan splits it into three payments: one eighty three sixty seven, one eighty three sixty seven, and one eighty three sixty six. Nothing was blocked, and Alexa speaks the answer.

slides.title: Grounding guard
slides.label: Simulated Alexa+ experience
lines: LLM draft: "You owe $551 in 3 payments of $183.67"   -> OK
Real bug we found and fixed: the LLM sent coinsurance=20 and
Server now normalizes percent and rejects impossible OOP values.
slides.say: Here's the guard. If the model drafts an amount that isn't in a tool result, like five hundred sixty dollars, the reply is blocked and Alexa reads the server's own sentence instead. And while testing we caught a real bug: the model sent coinsurance as twenty instead of zero point two, and an out-of-pocket value of zero as a placeholder, which made the bill zero. The server now normalizes those inputs, and there's a regression test for it.

slides.title: Care barriers screen
slides.label: Simulated Alexa+ experience
lines: $ python3 alexa_sim.py "I live in 78741, no car, I care for my mom,
money is tight. Who can help?"
Alexa: "We can help with transportation, cost, and caregiving..."
Strict schema (additionalProperties: false) -> no invented keys.
slides.say: The second question patients ask out loud: what's keeping me from my appointments? No car, I care for my mom, money is tight. The screener returns a high tier, flags transportation, cost and caregiving, and lists five resources and concrete actions. A strict schema stops the model from inventing answer keys, another bug we found and fixed.
